CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the recent adjustments in the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with particular attention to the efficacy of increased sertraline dosage and the overall impact on daily functioning.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a notable improvement in his anxiety symptoms following the recent increase in sertraline to 250 mg daily. He states that his anxiety has become more manageable, particularly in relation to work-related stressors, which has allowed him to engage more fully in his professional responsibilities. Mr. Smith mentions that he has been experiencing fewer nocturnal awakenings, with an average of 6-7 hours of uninterrupted sleep per night.
Despite this progress, he still experiences persistent fatigue, which he attributes to both the ongoing demands of his job and the residual effects of his anxiety. The patient reports that his tension-type headaches have decreased in frequency to approximately 1-2 times per week, with an intensity rating of 2-3 out of 10. He continues to use ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, but has noted a decrease in reliance on this medication.
Mr. Smith has maintained his bi-weekly acupuncture sessions and has incorporated yoga more regularly into his routine. He feels that these practices have contributed positively to his mental health, although he still struggles with occasional feelings of fatigue.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (increased) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (decreased usage) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (increased to twice weekly)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer and reports a better ability to manage stress with the current treatment plan. He remains active in his running group and has committed to attending yoga classes twice a week, which he finds beneficial for both physical and mental health. His dietary habits remain healthy, with continued abstinence from alcohol and minimal caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Improved anxiety levels; sleep quality has stabilized; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has decreased; intensity mild; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, though less pronounced; no fever or weight changes noted.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears slightly fatigued but engaged and in good spirits. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with reduced anxiety noted.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily given the positive response. Lorazepam usage is effective at 1 mg twice weekly as needed for acute anxiety episodes. Encourage ongoing participation in CBT and mindfulness practices. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 50 mg at bedtime and melatonin at 10 mg. Reinforce sleep hygiene practices to support continued improvement in sleep quality. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily. Monitor headache frequency and intensity, with a follow-up in two months to reassess treatment efficacy. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to continue physical activity, yoga, and mindfulness practices. Should fatigue persist or worsen, consider referral to a sleep specialist for further evaluation.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-01-01 to monitor ongoing symptoms, evaluate the effectiveness of the current treatment plan, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
